What we study

## One lab, four connected lines of inquiry

We work across the stroke-care continuum, linking population evidence to individual decisions and recovery.
:::

::: {.focus-grid}
::: {.focus-card}
::: {.card-number}
01
:::
### Prevention & outcomes
Risk prediction and prevention around surgery and neuroendovascular care, including an externally validated model for 30-day stroke risk.

[See the research →](research.qmd)
:::

::: {.focus-card}
::: {.card-number}
02
:::
### Cerebrovascular evidence
Nationwide datasets and international registries that clarify treatment, recurrence, and long-term outcomes after arterial and venous stroke.

[See the research →](research.qmd)
:::

::: {.focus-card}
::: {.card-number}
03
:::
### Imaging & NeuroAI
Clinical AI for imaging and unstructured health records, including automated abstraction of thrombectomy reports.

[See the research →](research.qmd)
:::

::: {.focus-card}
::: {.card-number}
04
:::
### Neurorecovery
Wearable sensing and machine learning to measure how stroke survivors use the affected arm in everyday activity.

[See the research →](research.qmd)
:::
:::
:::

## What the research has produced

These are findings from completed, peer-reviewed studies—not descriptions of work in progress.
:::

::: {.evidence-grid}
::: {.evidence-card}
::: {.evidence-stat}
≈445K
:::
**procedures across three hospitals**

An EHR-derived model predicted 30-day periprocedural ischemic stroke with an external-validation AUC of **0.86**.

[Read the 2026 JAHA paper →](https://doi.org/10.1161/JAHA.125.049372)
:::

::: {.evidence-card}
::: {.evidence-stat}
94.8%
:::
**best extraction accuracy**

Open-source language models converted **2,416 thrombectomy reports** into structured stroke-registry variables.

[Read the 2026 AJNR paper →](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41720514/)
:::

::: {.evidence-card}
::: {.evidence-stat}
3 cohorts
:::
**DIAS³ development and validation**

A six-variable clinical score estimated individualized 1- and 3-year epilepsy risk after cerebral venous thrombosis.

[Read the 2024 JAMA Neurology paper →](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39432281/)
:::

::: {.evidence-card}
::: {.evidence-stat}
92.6%
:::
**intrasubject model accuracy**

Machine learning distinguished functional from nonfunctional arm movement after stroke using wrist accelerometry.

[Read the rehabilitation study →](https://doi.org/10.1177/1545968320962483)
:::
:::

## Evidence you can open and explore

Two completed studies are available as public clinical decision-support tools.

[View all tools & resources](tools.qmd){.quiet-link}
:::

::: {.tools-preview-grid}
::: {.tool-preview-card}
::: {.tool-badge}
30-day procedural risk
:::
### Peri-procedural Stroke Risk Calculator
Estimate individualized 30-day ischemic-stroke risk using the externally validated Brown model.

[Open calculator ↗](https://liqi-shu.github.io/peri-procedural-stroke-calc/){.btn .btn-primary}
:::

::: {.tool-preview-card}
::: {.tool-badge}
1- and 3-year risk
:::
### DIAS³ Epilepsy Risk Calculator
Estimate epilepsy risk after cerebral venous thrombosis using the internationally validated DIAS³ score.

[Open calculator ↗](https://cerebralvenousthrombosis.com/professionals/dias-3/){.btn .btn-primary}
:::

## Built for useful answers

We pair methodological rigor with a bias toward deployable clinical value—risk stratification, prognostication, and workflow tools that can improve real decisions.

[Our research approach](research.qmd){.text-link-light}
:::

::: {.feature-pillars}
::: {.pillar}
**01 · Grounded**  
Questions begin with unmet needs in stroke care.
:::
::: {.pillar}
**02 · Collaborative**  
Clinicians, statisticians, engineers, and trainees work together.
:::
::: {.pillar}
**03 · Translational**  
Outputs are designed to move from analysis toward action.
:::
